top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori's magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, Ye's demonstration of 10^-18 accuracy and stability) is a mature, independently reproduced and surpassed achievement with a short two-person credit chain and a well-bounded citation. It opens new uses such as gravitational-potential sensing and tests of constant drift and dark-matter couplings, and it is a distinct step from the comb (2005) and single-ion control (2012) prizes. It is the only awarded configuration on the slate and clearly preferable to no award.
recusal_note: No direct conflict apparent from profile; I work in atomic theory and have computed atomic structure relevant to precision spectroscopy, but have no documented collaboration with Katori or Ye.
